placementQuiz.q: HyperLogLog (HLL) provides approximate distinct count with:
placementQuiz.explain: HyperLogLog uses fixed-size registers (e.g., 2^14 = 16KB) regardless of cardinality.
TDigest is a streaming percentile algorithm with bounded error (~1%) and O(1) memory.

placementQuiz.q: KMV (K Minimum Values) sketch is used for:
placementQuiz.explain: KMV maintains K minimum hash values — supports distinct count, top-K, and set operations.

options: Automatic background refresh with configurable lag
placementQuiz.explain: Continuous aggregates auto-refresh via background workers with configurable lag and schedule.

options: Streaming = push-based, continuous = pull-based with materialization
placementQuiz.explain: Streaming processes events as they arrive (push). Continuous aggregates materialize incrementally on schedule (pull).

blocks.md: **Exact COUNT(DISTINCT) = O(N) memory. Approximate = O(1) memory, ~1-2% error. HyperLogLog for distinct count, TDigest for percentiles, KMV for top-K. Essential for 1B+ row datasets.**

sections.title: Streaming Analytics — Continuous Views, PipelineDB, pg_streaming

blocks.label: continuous aggregate
blocks.code:
-- TimescaleDB continuous aggregate
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW hourly_events
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', time) AS bucket,
  device_id,
  COUNT(*) AS event_count,
  AVG(value) AS avg_value
FROM events
GROUP BY bucket, device_id;

-- Automatic refresh (background)
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('hourly_events',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '3 hours',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 hour',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 hour');

-- Real-time view (combines materialized + raw)
SELECT * FROM hourly_events WHERE bucket > now() - INTERVAL '1 day';

items.q: Seen from the query side, what does the lag (end_offset) of a continuous aggregate mean:
items.explain: end_offset = how far behind real-time the materialized summary trails; recent rows inside the lag window are served from the raw data, not the summary.
Real-time view = materialized (historical) + raw tail (recent data).

sections.title: Advanced Spatial Analytics — Parallel Spatial Joins, KNN, H3

blocks.label: parallel spatial join
blocks.code:
-- Parallel spatial join (PostgreSQL 13+)
SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 4;

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT a.id, b.id
FROM a
JOIN b ON ST_DWithin(a.geom, b.geom, 1000);
-- Plan shows: Parallel Seq Scan + Gather Merge

blocks.label: KNN search
blocks.code:
-- KNN: find 5 nearest neighbors
SELECT id, name, geom <-> ST_MakePoint(-122.4, 37.7) AS dist
FROM pois
ORDER BY geom <-> ST_MakePoint(-122.4, 37.7)
LIMIT 5;

-- GiST index required for <->
CREATE INDEX idx_pois_geom ON pois USING GIST (geom);

-- KNN with filter
SELECT * FROM pois
WHERE category = 'restaurant'
ORDER BY geom <-> ST_MakePoint(-122.4, 37.7)
LIMIT 10;
blocks.pg:
-- <-> = KNN distance operator (GiST index)
-- Supports LIMIT for early termination
blocks.py-pandas:
# Manual KNN with spatial index
from rtree import index
idx = index.Index()
for i, geom in enumerate(geoms): idx.insert(i, geom.bounds)
list(idx.nearest(point.bounds, 5))

blocks.md: **KNN <-> operator uses GiST index for O(log N) search.** Early termination with LIMIT avoids full scan. Composite index (category, geom) for filtered KNN.

items.explain: <-> operator requires GiST index on geometry column for O(log N) KNN search.
Parallel spatial join uses multiple workers, each processing a partition, then Gather Merge combines results.

-- Resolutions 0-15 (0=coarse, 15=finest ~1m²)

import h3
h3.latlng_to_cell(37.7749, -122.4194, 8)
# '8828308287fffff'

blocks.md: H3 advantages: equal area, hierarchical, constant-time neighbor lookup, efficient range queries. Resolution 8 = ~0.7km², Res 10 = ~15km².

blocks.label: h3 aggregation
blocks.code:
-- Aggregate events into H3 hexagons (resolution 8)
SELECT h3_lat_lng_to_cell(lat, lng, 8) AS hex,
       COUNT(*) AS event_count,
       AVG(value) AS avg_value
FROM events
WHERE ts > now() - INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY hex;

-- Join with cell boundaries for visualization
SELECT h.hex, h.count, h3_cell_to_boundary_wkt(h.hex) AS geom
FROM (
  SELECT h3_lat_lng_to_cell(lat, lng, 8) AS hex, COUNT(*)
  FROM events GROUP BY hex
) h;
blocks.py-pandas:
# h3-py
import h3
df['h3'] = df.apply(lambda r: h3.latlng_to_cell(r.lat, r.lng, 8), axis=1)
df.groupby('h3').agg(count=('id', 'count'), avg_val=('value', 'mean'))

items.explain: Resolution 8 ≈ 0.7 km² per hexagon. Resolution 10 ≈ 0.01 km² (10,000 m²).

revisionCard: HyperLogLog: O(1) memory, ~1-2% error for COUNT(DISTINCT). hll extension.
TDigest: streaming percentile algorithm, O(1) memory, ~1% error.
Continuous aggregates (TimescaleDB): auto-refreshed MV with incremental refresh.
Streaming aggregates: continuous view = materialized + raw tail; PipelineDB/pg_streaming.
KNN <-> operator: GiST index, O(log N) search, LIMIT for early termination.
H3 hexagons: hierarchical, equal-area, hierarchical. Res 8=0.7km², Res 10=15km².

glossary.def: Probabilistic algorithm for approximate distinct count with fixed memory.
Streaming percentile algorithm with O(1) memory and bounded error.
TimescaleDB: automatically maintained materialized view with incremental refresh.
PipelineDB/pg_streaming: real-time view combining materialized history + streaming tail.
K-Nearest Neighbors via GiST index and <-> operator (PostgreSQL).
Uber's hexagonal hierarchical grid system. Equal-area, hierarchical, constant-time neighbor lookup.
